# Preview checks (SEO / AEO / performance) — design

Date: 2026-11-14  
Status: draft for review  
Scope: `packages/astro` (rules, CI runner, in-page panel), template sync + deploy workflow.  
Supersedes (product approach): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-31-seo-audit-design.md` — that design’s daemon crawl + CMS **SEO** tab are not the path. Rule *ideas* from it are reused.

## Problem

Writers need publish-oriented feedback on the page they are looking at, and the same
bar must run when they Share preview / Publish so GitHub checks stay trustworthy.
Third-party Astro SEO plugins audit `dist/` for developers and do not plug into the
orso preview or agent loop. Duplicating rules in the daemon and in CI will drift.

## Goal

One rule pack owned by the **orso Astro plugin**, used in two places:

1. **In-page panel** inside the rendered Astro app during `astro dev` (the CMS preview
   iframe). This is the only writer-facing checks UI — no CMS SEO tab.
2. **CI** via the same plugin on `astro:build:done`, so `npm run build` in the site
   workflow produces a consistent check next to Deploy.

Success: a writer opens the panel on `/pricing/`, sees “missing meta description”,
fixes it (or asks the agent from the panel); later Share preview / Publish runs the
same rule against `dist/` and the PR checks strip stays green only when those rules
pass at the configured severity.

## Decisions

| # | Decision |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Orso owns the feature through `packages/astro` (`orso()`), not a third-party SEO integration and not a CMS-only Rust crawler. |
| 2 | Writer UI is **only** an in-page panel in the preview (injected into the Astro app). No `SeoPanel` route/tab in the CMS web app for v1. |
| 3 | CI checks live in the orso plugin (`astro:build:done` over `dist/`). The existing site `deploy.yml` keeps calling `npm run build`; the plugin fails or warns as part of that job. |
| 4 | Performance belongs in the **same** in-page panel (heuristics first), not a separate CMS module. |
| 5 | One shared rule module; both runners call it. Findings use stable `rule` ids so copy and severity match in panel and CI logs. |
| 6 | Panel injects in **`dev` only** (like today’s `bridge.js`). Production / Workers preview deploys do not ship the panel UI. |
| 7 | Default CI gate: **errors fail the build**; warnings print and do not fail. Configurable later; v1 can hard-code that split. |
| 8 | No Lighthouse / real CWV lab run in v1. Static HTML + light resource heuristics only. Full Lighthouse can be a later optional runner. |
| 9 | Steal check *ideas* from packages such as `@nuasite/checks` / `@casoon/astro-post-audit`; do not add them as template dependencies. |

## Architecture

```
packages/astro/src/
  checks/
    rules.js          # pure: HTML string (+ optional page URL) → Finding[]
    site.js           # cross-page / site files (robots, sitemap, duplicates)
    report.js         # shared formatting (terminal + panel JSON shape)
  panel/
    panel.js          # in-page UI + “run on this page” / summary
  index.js            # orso(): inject panel+bridge in dev; audit on build:done
  bridge.js           # existing pick/appearance; optional agent postMessage hook
```

Template copy stays the sync story: `just sync-orso-integration` →
`templates/astro-marketing/integrations/orso/`.

### Runner A — in-page panel (writer)

- Injected with `injectScript` during `astro:config:setup` when `command === "dev"`,
  same gate as `PREVIEW_BRIDGE`. May ship as one bundle with the bridge or a sibling
  IIFE; must not run meaningful work until the user opens the panel (or an explicit
  refresh), so preview stays snappy.
- Scope for v1: **current document** (`document.documentElement.outerHTML` / parsed
  DOM). Site-wide rules that need other pages (duplicate titles, crawl) are **CI /
  build only** in v1, or shown as “run a build to check site-wide” notes — do not
  crawl the whole site from the browser panel in v1.
- Panel chrome: collapsed trigger (e.g. corner control) → expanded drawer with
  summary counts and a list of findings for this page. Group by severity.
- Optional v1 stretch: **Fix with agent** posts a plain-language prompt to the parent
  via the existing preview `postMessage` channel (extend `bridge.js` / `frameBridge`),
  reusing the agent outbox. If that bridge work slips, the panel still ships as
  read-only findings.

### Runner B — CI (build)

- Hook `astro:build:done` (or equivalent that sees the final `dir` / pages).
- Walk HTML under the build output; run page rules per file; run site rules once
  (`robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml`, duplicate title/description across pages, broken
  internal links resolved against files on disk).
- Print a grouped report to stdout. Exit non-zero if any **error**-severity finding
  exists. Warnings never fail v1.
- No network fetch of external URLs. No headless browser.

CMS already aggregates GitHub check-runs on Share preview / Publish; a failed build
surfaces there without a new CMS findings UI.

## Findings model

Shared shape (panel JSON and CI log both derive from this):

```ts
type Finding = {
  rule: string;       // stable id, e.g. "description-missing"
  severity: "error" | "warning";
  page: string;       // path like "/" or "/pricing/" ; "." for site-wide
  message: string;    // plain language, no jargon in the headline
  detail?: string;    // optional examples (srcs, missing tags)
  count?: number;
};
```

CI may add file paths relative to `dist/` in the log line; the panel does not need
`dist` paths.

## Rules (v1)

### Per page (panel + CI)

| Rule | Severity | Fires when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title-missing` | error | No / blank `<title>` |
| `title-length` | warning | Title over 60 characters |
| `description-missing` | warning | No / blank meta description |
| `description-length` | warning | Description over 160 characters |
| `heading` | error / warning | No `h1` (error); more than one (warning) |
| `image-alt` | warning | `img` missing `alt` (empty `alt=""` allowed) |
| `html-lang` | warning | `<html>` missing non-blank `lang` |
| `social-preview` | warning | Missing `og:title`, `og:description`, or `og:image` |
| `noindex` | warning | Robots meta contains `noindex` |
| `canonical-missing` | warning | No `link[rel=canonical]` |
| `json-ld-missing` | warning | No JSON-LD script (document types that expect it can be tuned later; v1: warn if none on the page) |
| `json-ld-invalid` | error | JSON-LD present but not parseable JSON |

### AEO / answer-engine oriented (per page)

| Rule | Severity | Fires when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `json-ld-type` | warning | JSON-LD present but no useful `@type` among a small allowlist (`Organization`, `WebSite`, `WebPage`, `Article`, `BlogPosting`, `FAQPage`, `HowTo`, `BreadcrumbList`) |
| `faq-structure` | warning | Visible FAQ pattern (details/summary or heading+Q copy heuristics) without `FAQPage` JSON-LD — keep heuristic conservative; prefer skip over false positives |

### Performance heuristics (panel + CI; not Lighthouse)

| Rule | Severity | Fires when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `img-dimensions` | warning | `img` lacking both `width` and `height` |
| `sync-script` | warning | Render-blocking classic `script src` in `head` without `defer`/`async`/`type=module` |
| `huge-inline` | warning | Inline `<script>` or `<style>` over a size cap (e.g. 50 KiB) |

Panel may also show a simple **resource summary** for the current document (counts of
scripts, stylesheets, images, approx. HTML size). That summary is informational and
not a CI-failing rule unless mapped to a rule above.

### Site-wide (CI only in v1)

| Rule | Severity | Fires when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `broken-link` | error | Internal `a[href]` target missing from `dist` |
| `duplicate-title` | warning | Same non-blank title on multiple pages |
| `duplicate-description` | warning | Same non-blank description on multiple pages |
| `robots-missing` | warning | No `robots.txt` in output |
| `sitemap-missing` | warning | No `sitemap.xml` in output |

## Panel UX (preview)

- Collapsed by default; does not cover the page until opened.
- Shows findings for the **current URL** only; re-run on navigation or via a refresh
  control (listen to Astro view transitions / `popstate` / bridge `path` if needed).
- Copy matches CI rule messages where possible.
- Visual language: compact developer-tool drawer, readable in light and dark preview
  appearance modes (respect existing appearance bridge).
- Must not break element pick mode: when pick is active, panel interaction is disabled
  or the panel is collapsed.

## CI / template

- No new workflow file required if build already runs in
  `templates/astro-marketing/.github/workflows/deploy.yml`. Document that SEO/AEO
  errors fail `npm run build` via `orso()`.
- After implementation, sync the integration into the template so new and updated
  projects get the hooks.
- Forks / sites that vendor an old `integrations/orso` without checks will not get CI
  gating until they sync — acceptable; scaffolding and sync remain the distribution
  path (no separate npm publish required for v1 beyond the existing copy model).

## Relationship to the CMS app

- **No** new project tab, route, or `POST /api/seo/audit` for this feature in v1.
- Preview iframe already hosts the panel; Share preview / Publish already show check
  status from GitHub.
- Optional later: richer check annotations in the PR bar; out of scope here.

## Testing

**Plugin unit**

- Table-driven tests for each rule over HTML fixtures (missing title, long description,
  bad JSON-LD, image without alt, etc.).
- Build-hook test: temp `dist/` with one good and one bad page → expect error exit and
  finding ids.
- Integration test updates: `astro build` is no longer a total no-op for checks; assert
  the hook runs and that **dev** still injects the panel/bridge while **build** does
  not inject panel UI into output HTML.

**Manual / e2e (lightweight)**

- Open CMS preview, open panel, confirm a known missing description appears.
- Optional e2e can wait until the panel has stable `data-testid`s.

## Out of scope

- CMS SEO tab, daemon HTML crawler API, saved report history.
- Lighthouse, lab CWV, full axe/Playwright a11y (may return as a later runner).
- External link checking, Search Console, rankings.
- Shipping the panel into production or Workers preview deployments.
- Editing the starter template’s default SEO assets (robots/sitemap/OG) — follow-up so
  new projects start clean under the new CI rules.
- Requiring a hosted orso service for CI.

## Migration note

Mark `2026-10-31-seo-audit-design.md` as **superseded for product UX and ownership**
(point here). Keep it as historical reference for rule copy and severity choices that
this spec reuses.

**Understood:** you want the checks UI itself to be Vue + shadcn, living in the Astro preview so it *looks* like orso.

**Constraint:** shadcn in this repo lives in `web/` (Vite/Vue app). The preview is a separate Astro app. You can’t `import` those components into `packages/astro` without a dedicated build that **vendors** Vue + a shadcn subset into the inject bundle.

### Realistic options

**1. Inject a tiny Vue+shadcn mini-app (what you described)**  
- New package/build: Vue + Button/Badge/etc. → one ESM  
- `orso()` injects that bundle in `dev`  
- Styles stay consistent only if you keep that package in sync with `web/`  
- Cost: build step, duplicate design-system surface, larger inject  

**2. Vue+shadcn overlay in `PreviewPanel` (recommended for real reuse)**  
- Uses the **same** `web/` shadcn components — no copy  
- Sits on the preview visually; audit via DOM or bridge  
- Styling can’t drift  

**3. Keep inject, match tokens only (current)**  
- Looks close; not Vue/shadcn  

For “reuse the project’s shadcn,” **2** is the only one that reuses the real components. **1** reuses the *look* via a second build.

Which do you want: **inject a vendored Vue panel (1)** or **orso overlay with real shadcn (2)**?

Yes — technically possible, but it’s a worse fit than the current Astro plugin injection for this panel.

**Today:** `orso()` injects the panel with Astro’s `injectScript` during `astro:config:setup`. The daemon preview proxy ([`src/preview.rs`](src/preview.rs)) deliberately **does not rewrite HTML**; it only forwards `/preview/{id}/*` and tunnels Vite HMR.

**Proxy injection would mean:** detect `text/html`, buffer the body, splice in a `<script type="module">` (or similar) that loads the panel from the daemon, fix `Content-Length` / strip encoding, and skip non-HTML (assets, WS, 101).

| | Plugin (current) | Proxy inject |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Works without orso in the site | No | Yes |
| Survives Astro/Vite HMR cleanly | Yes (Astro owns it) | Fragile (rewriting + streaming) |
| Same panel in bare `astro dev` / CI story | Yes | No (CMS-only) |
| Complexity | Low | High (HTML parse, gzip, CSP, partial responses) |

**Recommendation:** keep the panel in the plugin. Use the proxy only if the goal is “any upstream site, even without `orso()`.”

If you want that CMS-only path later, the clean shape is: daemon serves `checks-panel.js`, proxy injects one module tag on HTML — and keep `readPageMeta` / rules in the shared package either way.
Because I have hoping to not go through npm to distrubute the plugin
That clarifies the motivation — I'll check how the plugin is wired today and outline ways to ship the panel without an npm package.

That goal already matches the direction you’re on — **don’t publish `orso-astro` to npm**. The product decision was: **vendor** runtime into `integrations/orso/` (shadcn-style copy), with `packages/astro` staying the in-repo source of truth.

Proxy injection doesn’t replace that whole plugin. It only helps one piece.

| Need | Needs site-side code? | Proxy can own it? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Page details panel in CMS preview | No, if proxy injects | Yes |
| Pick / appearance bridge | Soft — parent postMessage | Possible via proxy |
| Content catalog / `__orso` patch | Yes | No |
| CI checks on `astro build` | Yes (`astro:build:done`) | No |

So: **proxy = “orso chrome over any Astro preview”**; **vendored `integrations/orso` = “site is orso-aware”** (edit + publish checks). Avoiding npm doesn’t require the proxy — the copy model already does that.

**Practical split**
1. Keep shipping the integration as **copied files**, not an npm package (finish/lean on that path; drop `file:packages/astro` / `sync:orso-astro` on live sites when you can).
2. Optionally **also** inject the panel from the daemon proxy later, so preview works even when a project hasn’t vendored the panel yet — still serve `checks-panel.js` from the daemon, not npm.

If the pain is “I don’t want users to `npm install orso-astro`,” you’re already designing the right answer with **copy-into-project**, not proxy-only.

# Page details as preview sidebar (orso app)

## Decision

Replace the iframe floating **Page details** popup with a **collapsible sidebar inside the CMS preview UI**, toggled from the existing preview toolbar ([`web/src/modules/preview/PreviewPanel.vue`](web/src/modules/preview/PreviewPanel.vue)).

This matches the earlier goal: users do not get a minified Vue bundle in their repo. The UI lives in orso; sites only keep readable `integrations/orso/checks/` for CI.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  header[Preview toolbar button]
  sidebar[Page details sidebar]
  iframe[Preview iframe same-origin]
  rules[readPageMeta + auditPage]
  header -->|toggle| sidebar
  sidebar -->|read contentDocument| iframe
  sidebar --> rules
```

## UX

- New toolbar control next to appearance / pick (e.g. `ListTree` / `FileSearch`): **Page details**.
- Opens a **right-hand sidebar** within the preview panel (not a modal over the site). Collapses closed by default.
- Sidebar content: same SEO snapshot (title, description, canonical, robots, lang, H1, OG, JSON-LD) + findings list + **Fix this** (existing `op: "fix"` → agent outbox).
- Resource summary line stays at the top of the sidebar.
- Badge on the toolbar icon for error/warning counts when collapsed (same idea as today’s FAB counts).

## Data (no site panel inject)

Preview is same-origin via the daemon (`/preview/{id}/…` on the app host), so on iframe `load` / path change / Refresh, the parent reads `iframe.contentDocument` and runs:

- `readPageMeta(doc)`
- `auditPage(doc, { path })`

Port the readable check modules into the web app (e.g. [`web/src/modules/preview/checks/`](web/src/modules/preview/checks/) copied or shared from [`packages/astro/src/checks/`](packages/astro/src/checks/) — plain JS/TS, no Vue). ## Cleanup (plugin / template)

- Remove Astro `injectScript` of `checks-panel.js` from [`packages/astro/src/index.js`](packages/astro/src/index.js).
- Stop syncing/vendoring [`panel/checks-panel.js`](packages/astro/src/panel/checks-panel.js) into templates/scaffolds (leave `panel-ui` in-repo only if you still want a local playground, or delete later).
- Keep `bridge.js` inject for pick/appearance until those move too.
- Keep `astro:build:done` + readable `checks/` for CI.

## Out of scope

- Full HTML-rewriting proxy inject (unnecessary once the UI is in orso).
- Editing SEO fields in the sidebar (Fix this → agent remains the write path).
- Moving pick/appearance off the site bridge.

What's a simple way to do AB testing ?

Simplest depends what you’re testing:

**Marketing copy / SEO (astro-marketing)**  
Don’t bolt on an experiment stack yet. Ship **two URLs or two PRs**, send half the traffic each (ads, LinkedIn, email), compare in Search Console / Cloudflare analytics. Privacy page already says no first-party analytics — that stays honest.

**In-product UI (orso)**  
A boolean in settings or a `?variant=` / localStorage flag is enough for you + early users. Measure with a single event (“opened Page details”, “clicked Fix this”) if you care.

**Real split traffic later**  
PostHog or GrowthBook feature flags: assign A/B once, stick it in a cookie, render variant in Astro/Vue. Worth it only when you need stats, not vibes.

For launch: **two variants + traffic split by channel** beats wiring experiments. What are you trying to A/B — landing copy, or something in the app?

# Turn-end commit subjects from the agent

## Why it is not “out of the box” today

Interactive Claude Code / Cursor / Codex often draft commit messages when *they* run `git commit` (or a `/commit`-style flow).

In Orso that path is mostly unused:

- Turn end always runs [`finish_turn`](src/http/checkpoints.rs) → [`git::checkpoint`](src/git.rs), which commits dirty files as `checkpoint: <summary>`.
- `<summary>` comes from [`commit_message`](src/http/checkpoints.rs): optional `COMMIT:` line, else **first line of the agent chat reply**, else a file list.
- Recent History rows (`I'll find…`, `Removed that note…`) are those Orso checkpoints (author = you), not CLI-native commit drafts. The transcript for those turns had **no** `COMMIT:` lines, so fallback won.

So the coding CLI never gets asked for a commit message; Orso invents one from chat.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant User
  participant Agent
  participant Orso
  participant Git
  User->>Agent: edit request
  Agent->>Git: optional mid-turn commits (rare in practice)
  Agent-->>User: chat reply
  Note over Orso: turn_end
  Orso->>Git: checkpoint dirty tree with chat-derived subject
```

## Goal

When a normal (non-sync) chat turn ends and the tree is dirty, the checkpoint subject should be an **imperative one-liner describing the change**, produced by the same agent session—not the first sentence of the reply.

## Approach

**Ask once at turn end (hidden), then checkpoint.**

1. In [`wire_chat_turn_end`](src/state.rs) (after preview/content refresh, before `finish_turn`):
   - If `git::changed_paths` is empty → unchanged; skip ask.
   - Else call a new `ChatManager` API on the **same** live chat, e.g. `draft_checkpoint_subject(project, chat, &files) -> Option<String>`:
     - Hidden ACP prompt (no user bubble), e.g. list changed paths and require a single line `COMMIT: …` (imperative, ≤72 chars, no chatter).
     - Await that prompt’s text with a **short timeout** (e.g. 15–20s); on cancel/error/timeout → `None`.
     - **Do not** record the draft turn’s text/turn_end into the visible transcript (or record nothing user-facing); **do not** re-enter the checkpoint hook for that draft turn (flag / `TurnEnded` kind / skip `note_turn_end` hook when drafting).
   - Pass `draft.or(ended.summary)` into `finish_turn` (existing `COMMIT:` parse + fallbacks remain).

2. Keep the `COMMIT:` convention in [`ORSO_GUIDE`](src/providers.rs) as a soft help; the turn-end ask is the reliable path.

3. Tests:
   - Unit: `commit_message` still prefers `COMMIT:` (already covered).
   - Manager/integration: draft prompt returns subject used by checkpoint; timeout/failure falls back; draft turn does not nest another checkpoint; sync chats unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Rewriting old History rows.
- Relying only on mid-turn agent `git commit` (agents rarely do it here; Orso still must cover leftovers).
- Showing the draft Q&A in the chat UI.
